articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually left AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub because apparently 'cybersecurity' doesn't apply to the cybersecurity agency itself. The irony is so thick you could patch vulnerabilities with it.

articles.title: Fake Android Apps Commit Carrier Billing Fraud for Premium Services
articles.summary: GitHub got pwned by TeamPCP who stole 4K internal repos via a poisoned VS Code extension. When the house of code gets its own code stolen, you know we're living in peak timeline.

articles.title: Microsoft storms RAMPART, adds Clarity to agentic AI safety
articles.summary: Cisco serves up another perfect 10 CVSS vulnerability in Secure Workload because 'secure' is apparently just marketing speak. Attackers can hop tenant boundaries like they're playing cybersecurity hopscotch.

articles.title: When Identity is the Attack Path
articles.summary: Microsoft Defender has two actively exploited vulns including a privilege escalation to SYSTEM. The irony of the defender needing defending writes itself.

articles.title: GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension
articles.summary: A 9-year-old Linux kernel flaw finally surfaces, proving that some bugs age like fine wine—getting more dangerous with time. CVE-2026-46333 lets unprivileged users party with sensitive data.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a win for encrypted messaging while governments worldwide continue their eternal tantrum about not being able to read our DMs. End-to-end encryption: making authoritarians cry since forever.

articles.title: Chinese APTs Share Linux Backdoor in Central Asia Telco Attacks
articles.summary: EFF drops a guide on fighting digital surveillance because apparently we need step-by-step instructions to not normalize living in a panopticon. The Americas' surveillance state needs some serious pushback.

articles.title: Even Claude agrees: hole in its sandbox was real and dangerous
articles.summary: Zombie user accounts let hackers control city water systems because basic IT hygiene is apparently optional for critical infrastructure. Someone forgot to disable ex-employee access—rookie mistake with catastrophic potential.

articles.title: Implement agentic AI in cybersecurity with Tenable Hexa AI: Reduce cyber risk at machine speed
articles.summary: P2PInfect botnet turns misconfigured Kubernetes clusters into its personal zombie army via exposed Redis instances. Cloud-native malware for the containerized apocalypse—how delightfully modern.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Linux Rootkits, Router 0-Day, AI Intrusions, Scam Kits and 25 New Stories
articles.summary: Claude AI's sandbox had a real dangerous hole that got silently patched with zero public disclosure. Even the AI admits its own security was trash—at least it's honest about being vulnerable.
